gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-003 identifies an incorrect boundary value in a Case A equality-condition list, whereas the gold issue is the missing converse proving that an admissible three-cluster configuration attains the equality singular-value bound. It does not recognize the omitted sufficiency direction.

ISSUE-001 gives the same counterexample showing that pairwise non-collinearity of three square vectors does not imply pairwise non-collinearity of their pair sums, and connects parallel sums to coincident singular directions, directly refuting Lemma le's conclusion.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The lemma falsely infers pairwise distinct pair sums and hence pairwise distinct singular directions from pairwise non-collinearity of the original square vectors.

component_coverage.gold_component: The claimed implication from pairwise non-collinear square vectors to pairwise non-collinear pair sums is false.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction supplies the same explicit vectors and shows two pair sums are parallel.

component_coverage.gold_component: The false pair-sum conclusion invalidates the claim that all three associated row-pair matrices have distinct right-singular directions.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly links parallel sums to the same first right-singular vector and states that the lemma is contradicted.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-001 concerns a false geometric implication about pair-sum collinearity. Although it invokes the angle formula, it does not identify that the one-argument arctangent is undefined when its denominator vanishes or loses quadrant information, nor does its repair provide a branch-safe atan2 formula.
